      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9()+\-.\s]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner registered. Defaults to the server's current date when omitted.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allows creating this owner even though another owner
            already has the same last name and address (they knowingly share a
            household). Not persisted.
          type: boolean
          default: false
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: Franklin, George
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:

## Change: `sharesHousehold` → shared `householdId`

The `sharesHousehold` opt-in already existed (it suppressed the `DuplicateHouseholdException`), but it did not produce a shared household identifier. I added that, keeping each concern in its natural place:

**1. Stable ID derivation — `util/HouseholdIdGenerator.java` (new)**
A small, single-purpose utility that derives the household identifier as a deterministic SHA-256 digest of the normalized `lastName` + `address` pair (reusing the existing `TextNormalizer`). Because it's deterministic, every member of a household computes the same value and it never drifts — i.e. genuinely "stable and shared."

**2. Persistence of the join — `ClinicService` / `ClinicServiceImpl`**
Added `joinHousehold(owner, existingMembers)`: it stamps the new owner with the household ID and back-fills any existing member that doesn't yet carry it (persisting only those that changed), returning the ID. This lives in the service/transactional layer where repository writes belong.

**3. Orchestration — `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`**
Refactored so the household lookup runs once; when `sharesHousehold` is true it delegates to `joinHousehold` before saving, otherwise it still throws `DuplicateHouseholdException` on a conflict. No duplicated logic.

**4. Model & wire format**
- `Owner` gains a `householdId` field mapped to a new `household_id` column.
- `household_id` added to all four schema files (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres).
- `householdId` added as a read-only property on the `Owner` schema in `openapi.yml`, so the generated `OwnerDto` and MapStruct mapper expose it automatically — that's how `GET /api/owners/{id}` returns it.

The acceptance test `coreJoinersShareHouseholdId` (joiners `b` and `c` receive the same non-blank `householdId`) passes, and the full suite is green.
